Abelian_Variety.title: Abelian Variety
Abelian_Variety.define: An abelian variety is a complete algebraic group variety, central in arithmetic geometry.

Affine_Space.title: Affine Space
Affine_Space.define: An affine space is a geometric space with no distinguished origin.

Cone.title: Cone
Cone.define: A cone is a subset closed under multiplication by positive scalars.

Convex_Set.title: Convex Set
Convex_Set.define: A convex set is a subset that contains the line segment joining any two of its points.

Differential_Manifold.title: Differential Manifold
Differential_Manifold.define: A smooth manifold is a space that locally looks like $\mathbb R^n$, and whose overlapping coordinate systems transform smoothly into one another.

Elliptic_Curve.title: Elliptic Curve
Elliptic_Curve.define: An elliptic curve is a smooth projective genus-one curve with a chosen rational point, equivalently an abelian variety of dimension one.

Euclidean_Space.title: Euclidean Space
Euclidean_Space.define: Euclidean space is the standard model of flat finite-dimensional geometry.

Fractal.title: Fractal
Fractal.define: A fractal is a geometric object whose structure exhibits detail across scales, often through self-similarity.

Hausdorff_Space.title: Hausdorff Space
Hausdorff_Space.define: A Hausdorff space is a topological space in which any two distinct points can be separated by disjoint neighborhoods.

Hilbert_Space.title: Hilbert Space
Hilbert_Space.define: A Hilbert space is a complete inner product space where geometric notions such as length and angle support limits.

Linear_Space.title: Linear Space
Linear_Space.define: A linear space is a set whose elements can be added and scaled by elements of a field.

Manifold.title: Manifold
Manifold.define: A manifold is a space that may be globally curved or complicated but locally looks like Euclidean space.

Modular_Curve.title: Modular Curve
Modular_Curve.define: A modular curve is an algebraic curve that parametrizes elliptic curves equipped with level structure.

Polyhedron.title: Polyhedron
Polyhedron.define: A polyhedron is a solid in three-dimensional space bounded by finitely many polygonal faces.

Projective_Space.title: Projective Space
Projective_Space.define: Projective space is the space of lines through the origin of a vector space.

Real_Field.title: Real Field
Real_Field.define: The real field is the complete ordered field that models the continuous number line.

Riemannian_Manifold.title: Riemannian Manifold
Riemannian_Manifold.define: A Riemannian manifold is a smooth manifold equipped with a positive definite metric tensor.

Scheme.title: Scheme
Scheme.define: A scheme is a space obtained by gluing together spectra of commutative rings.

Set.title: Set
Set.define: A set is a collection of distinct objects considered as a single mathematical object.

Sheaf.title: Sheaf
Sheaf.define: A sheaf is a device for assigning local data to open sets in a way that can be uniquely glued from compatible local pieces.

Simplex.title: Simplex
Simplex.define: A simplex is the simplest convex polytope in a given dimension.

Symplectic_Manifold.title: Symplectic Manifold
Symplectic_Manifold.define: A symplectic manifold is a smooth manifold equipped with a closed nondegenerate differential 2-form.

Tensor.title: Tensor
Tensor.define: A tensor is a multilinear object that generalizes scalars, vectors, covectors, and linear maps.

Topological_Space.title: Topological Space
Topological_Space.define: Topological Space is a space in which open sets are defined.
